plan.notes: Source: official UIC 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog (Volume 49, May 15, 2026), 'BS in Computer Science' page: https://catalog.uic.edu/ucat/colleges-depts/engineering/cs/bs-cs/ . Transcription method: manual transcription of the Degree Requirements tables and the official 'Sample Course Schedule' (Plan of Study Grid) from that catalog page on 2026-09-30. Course titles, credit hours, and prerequisites are from the catalog's official course descriptions (https://catalog.uic.edu/ucat/course-descriptions/cs/ and .../math/); ENGL 160/161 placement/prereq basis from the official UIC ECE curriculum document. CAVEATS: (1) The catalog's sample schedule leaves 21 cells blank (elective slots) without labeling which requirement category each fills; each is transcribed as a choice:true slot, and the category assignment per term (5 GenEd category courses, 2 CS-department-approved humanities/social sciences/art electives, 2 science electives, 6 technical electives, 3 required-math, 3 free electives) is the collector's inference from the Degree Requirements totals, not stated on the catalog page. (2) ENGR 100 is a 1-hour course, but per the catalog footnote its hour does not count toward the 128 required for graduation; it is transcribed as a required_zero 0-counting-credit slot so the credit sum matches the catalog's 128 total. (3) CS 499 is a genuine 0-credit course (S/U, seniors only, last semester). (4) Prereqs use catalog-listed course prereqs; 'credit or concurrent registration' allowances noted per slot. (5) MATH 121 appears only as an alternative prerequisite for MATH 180 (placement test also satisfies) and is listed under external_prereqs, not as a plan course.

courses.title: Program Design I
courses.choice_note: Take CS 111 (Program Design I), CS 112 (Program Design I in the Context of Biological Problems), or CS 113 (Program Design I in the Context of Law and Public Policy).

courses.title: Academic Writing I: Writing in Academic and Public Contexts
Science Elective (choice)
courses.choice_note: Every student must take two courses (8 hours total) from the catalog's Science Electives list; all are approved for the Analyzing the Natural World General Education category. General Education credit for CHEM 122/123 or CHEM 124/125 requires completing both parts.

courses.title: Engineering Success Seminar for Freshmen
courses.choice_note: Freshmen take ENGR 100; transfer students take ENGR 101 within their first semester after enrolling. Catalog footnote: ENGR 100/101 are one-semester-hour courses, but the hour does not count toward the 128 total hours required for graduation, so it carries 0 counting credits here.
